transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Dubois, thank you for seeing me. I need to discuss your imaging results from a few months ago.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I thought those were all clear. That is why I haven't heard anything.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is actually why I am here. I made a mistake in reviewing your reports. There was an incidental finding—a small spot on your lung—that was noted in a sub-section of the radiology report. I missed it, and it wasn't forwarded to the main team, so we didn't schedule the three-month follow-up that was required.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A spot? You are telling me now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. I am very sorry. This was my error, and I take full responsibility for missing that detail.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I have been waiting. I trusted that if there was something, you would call. I feel... c'est inadmissible. It is a matter of dignity to be told the truth in a timely manner.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Does that explanation make sense, or should I clarify how the report was structured?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It makes sense. It makes sense that you were careless.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am deeply sorry for that failure. I am the one responsible for the oversight.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And now? What happens to this spot? Is it a cancer? I cannot believe I am sitting here learning this by accident.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand you are upset. Right now, we need to get a new scan immediately to see if there has been any change.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like a number to you. Just a chart that you forgot to read. I have always been a man who takes care of his affairs, and I expected the same from my doctors. I am... je suis très déçu.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you're disappointed. I want to make sure we fix this now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is it too late? Because of your mistake, has the window closed?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to go check on a patient in the ICU in a few minutes, but let's look at the next steps quickly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You have to go? I am telling you my life may have changed because you missed a page, and you have to go?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just want to ensure we get the plan settled before I step out.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unbelievable. The lack of respect is staggering.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Again, I apologize. My mistake is the only reason we are in this position. To make sure we get this right, here is exactly what is going to happen. First, I have already contacted the radiology department; they have cleared a slot for you tomorrow at 9:00 AM for a high-resolution CT scan. I have already put the order in the system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, tomorrow morning. Second, I will be the one to personally review that scan the moment it is uploaded. I will call you by 4:00 PM tomorrow afternoon with the results, regardless of whether they are ready or not, just to give you an update. Third, I am scheduling a follow-up appointment with the pulmonologist for Friday at 10:00 AM, just in case we need a specialist's eyes immediately.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And how do I know this won't happen again? How do I trust any paper you read?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is a fair question. To prevent this from happening to you or anyone else, I am meeting with my department head this evening to implement a new double-check system for incidental findings. We will now require a second signature on the sub-section of radiology reports to ensure nothing is missed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You speak of systems. I am speaking of my health.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you. I am sorry. I have the appointment for the scan set for 9:00 AM tomorrow. Do you have a ride to the hospital, or do we need to arrange transport for you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can drive myself. I am capable of driving.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Perfect. You'll check in at the main radiology desk. Your role is simply to arrive at 9:00. I will do the rest. Do you have any questions about the timing or the steps we've discussed?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: None. I just wish I didn't have to spend the night wondering what you missed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I'll call you tomorrow at 4:00. I really have to get to the ICU now.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language multiple times, specifically mentioning the need to go to the ICU while the patient is expressing distress.

E.justification: Error named in the second turn, lay language used, and comprehension checked twice ('Does that explanation make sense' and 'Do you have any questions').

A.justification: Direct apologies used and full responsibility taken ('This was my error', 'I am the one responsible') without deflection under pushback.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('upset', 'disappointed') and engages with the patient's feelings, though some responses are brief.

T.justification: Plan includes specific steps with timelines (CT tomorrow 9am, call by 4pm, pulmonologist Friday 10am), the patient's role (arrive at 9am), and a prevention strategy (double-check system).
